58423-eight-girls-and-a-dog.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Now I know that a story with eight heroines is an imposition upon even the gentlest of readers; but you see there were eight girls in the Blue Ribbon Cooking Club; and when their president, Marjorie Bond, proposed that they go down to Long Beach and spend a fortnight all by themselves in her father’s cottage, the whole club rose up as one girl and voted aye.

arxiv-1601-05235.title: Beam–Beam Effects
arxiv-1601-05235.creator: W. Herr and T. Pieloni
arxiv-1601-05235.description: Abstract One of the most severe limitations in high-intensity particle colliders is the beam–beam interaction, i.e. the perturbation of the beams as they cross the opposing beams. This introduction to beam–beam effects concentrates on a description of the phenomena that are present in modern colliding beam facilities. 0.

arxiv-1911-01626.creator: Jason Li
arxiv-1911-01626.description: Abstract We present the first m ​ polylog ​ ( n ) m\,\text{polylog}(n) work, polylog ​ ( n ) \text{polylog}(n) time algorithm in the PRAM model that computes ( 1 + ϵ ) (1+\epsilon) -approximate single-source shortest paths on weighted, undirected graphs.

arxiv-2105-09365.title: Exploring the Limits of Data Augmentation For Retinal Vessel Segmentation
arxiv-2105-09365.creator: E. Sadi Uysal, M. Şafak Bilici, B. Selin Zaza, M. Yiğit Özgenç, Onur Boyar
arxiv-2105-09365.description: Abstract Retinal Vessel Segmentation is important for the diagnosis of various diseases. The research on retinal vessel segmentation focuses mainly on the improvement of the segmentation model which is usually based on U-Net [1] architecture. In our study, we use the U-Net architecture and we rely on heavy data augmentation in order to achieve better performance.

arxiv-2106-15640.title: Maximally twisted eleven-dimensional supergravity
arxiv-2106-15640.creator: Richard Eager, Fabian Hahner
arxiv-2106-15640.description: Abstract We perform the maximal twist of eleven-dimensional supergravity. This twist is partially topological and exists on manifolds of G 2 × S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) G_{2}\times SU(2) holonomy. Our derivation starts with an explicit description of the Batalin-Vilkovisky complex associated to the three-form multiplet in the pure spinor superfield formalism.

arxiv-2109-14961.title: Hyperbolic plane curves near the non-singular tropical limit
arxiv-2109-14961.creator: Cédric Le Texier
arxiv-2109-14961.description: Abstract . We determine necessary and sufficient conditions for real algebraic curves near the non-singular tropical limit to be hyperbolic with respect to a point, thus generalising Speyer’s classification of stable curves near the tropical limit. In order to obtain the conditions, we develop tools of real tropical intersection theory.

arxiv-2208-09954.title: Discovering neutrinoless double-beta decay in the era of precision neutrino cosmology
arxiv-2208-09954.creator: Manuel Ettengruber, Matteo Agostini, Allen Caldwell, Philipp Eller, Oliver Schulz
arxiv-2208-09954.description: Abstract We evaluate the discovery probability of a combined analysis of proposed neutrinoless double-beta decay experiments in a scenario with normal ordered neutrino masses. The discovery probability strongly depends on the value of the lightest neutrino mass, ranging from zero in case of vanishing masses and up to 80-90% for values just below the current constraints.

arxiv-2301-11454.title: Boundary Aware U-Net for Glacier Segmentation
arxiv-2301-11454.creator: Bibek Aryal, Katie E. Miles, Sergio A. Vargas Zesati, Olac Fuentes
arxiv-2301-11454.description: Abstract Large-scale study of glaciers improves our understanding of global glacier change and is imperative for monitoring the ecological environment, preventing disasters, and studying the effects of global climate change. Glaciers in the Hindu Kush Himalaya (HKH) are particularly interesting as the HKH is one of the world’s most sensitive regions for climate change.

arxiv-2311-16184.title: Impact of overlapping signals on parameterized post-Newtonian coefficients in tests of gravity Facilities: Einstein Telescope
arxiv-2311-16184.creator: Yixuan Dang, Ziming Wang, Dicong Liang, Lijing Shao
arxiv-2311-16184.description: Abstract Gravitational waves have been instrumental in providing deep insights into the nature of gravity. Next-generation detectors, such as the Einstein Telescope, are predicted to have a higher detection rate given the increased sensitivity and lower cut-off frequency. However, this increased sensitivity raises challenges concerning parameter estimation due to the foreseeable overlap of signals from multiple sources.

arxiv-2510-09604.title: Catalog of Mock Stellar Streams in Milky Way-like Galaxies ⋆ E-mail: cphh@umich.edu
arxiv-2510-09604.creator: Colin Holm-Hansen ⋆, Yingtian Chen, Oleg Y. Gnedin
arxiv-2510-09604.description: Abstract Dynamically cold stellar streams from tidally dissolved globular clusters (GCs) serve as excellent tools to measure the Galactic mass distribution and show promise to probe the nature of dark matter. For successful application of these tools to observations, it is essential to have an accurate model of stellar stream properties on the Galactic scale.

arxiv-2512-18330.title: Learning Generalized Nash Equilibria in Non-Monotone Games with Quadratic Costs
arxiv-2512-18330.creator: Tatiana Tatarenko, Lucas Wey Hacker
arxiv-2512-18330.description: Abstract We study generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problems in games with quadratic costs and individual linear equality constraints. Departing from approaches that require strong monotonicity and/or shared constraints, we reformulate the KKT conditions of the (generally non-monotone) games into a tractable convex program whose objective satisfies the Polyak–Łojasiewicz (PL) condition.
